[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · من العلماء | reports | Some scholars treat ṭāghūt as a foreign word on the pattern fāʿūl; al-Itqān says it means ‘soothsayer’ in Abyssinian, and Ibn Ḥajar added it to Ibn al-Subkī’s list of Quranic loanwords. | mentions 4:51
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | In Quran and Sunna, ṭāghūt denotes a powerful force in unbelief or oppression: an idol, a group of idols, or a leader of unbelievers such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf; here it means idols collectively.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The plural ṭawāghīt reflects predominance of its nominal use, though a single idol is an uncommon referent; feminine ‘worship them’ treats it as a nonrational plural.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The feminine pronoun for ṭāghūt agrees with its sense as a nonrational plural; 2:257 uses masculine agreement because it is predicated of masculine plural ‘allies’ or treated as rational by its worshippers. | mentions 2:257
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The clause ‘that they worship them’ is a بدل اشتمال (inclusive apposition) of ṭāghūt.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Ināba means repentance, as at 11:75; here it means repenting from every sin, above all from the pre-Islamic shirk they practiced. | mentions 11:75
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Bushrā means good news; here it is the good news of Paradise, as in the phrase about good news in this life and the next at 10:64. | mentions 10:64

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The good-news command refers to those who avoided ṭāghūt; replacing ‘announce to them’ with ‘announce to My servants’ and a relative clause adds praise for devotion to God and hearing and following the best speech.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · العشرة ما عدا السوسي | reports | All ten readers except al-Sūsī read ʿibādi with kasra on dāl and no yāʾ, a lightening that relies on the kasra.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · السوسي | reports | Al-Sūsī reads a yāʾ after dāl, open in connected reading and silent at pause; deletion at pause is also reported and both forms are grammatical, though the codices omit the yāʾ, weakening the reading unless treated as performance.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd says the verses were revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who avoided idol worship in pre-Islamic times and followed the best teaching that reached them.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the good-news passage was revealed about ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who came to Abū Bakr after his conversion, heard his testimony, and believed.

[TABATABAI:39:16-18/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Avoiding false worship alone is insufficient; what benefits people is both negation and affirmation: worshipping God alone and sincerely leaving every other object of worship.
